_chevron\_right_

• Text translation: Translate between 108 languages by typing

• Tap to Translate: Copy text in any app and tap the Google Translate icon to translate (all languages)

• Offline: Translate with no internet connection (59 languages)

• Instant camera translation: Translate text in images instantly by just pointing your camera (94 languages)

• Photos: Take or import photos for higher quality translations (90 languages)

• Conversations: Translate bilingual conversations on the fly (70 languages)

• Handwriting: Draw text characters instead of typing (96 languages)

• Phrasebook: Star and save translated words and phrases for future reference (all languages)

• Cross-device syncing: Login to sync phrasebook between app and desktop

• Transcribe: Continuously translate someone speaking a different language in near real-time (8 languages)

Permissions Notice

Google Translate may ask for the following optional permissions\*:

• Microphone for speech translation

• Camera for translating text via the camera

• External storage for downloading offline translation data

it's decent at translating, but the conversation feature has one annoying bug. if it is on the default setting, it translates what you say, then starts reading it out loud, but then it starts translating its own voice in a loop, repeating what you said in both languages until you pause it. you can avoid this by switching to text only, and it would be better if that was the default setting.

I have loved and used Google translate for years, but it has changed and I don't know how to change it back. there had been too small boxes, the top one for the language you speak in the bottom one the translation in whatever language you had asked for. now my Google translate is one long box and it is very user unfriendly. When I try to get it to simply speak what I had written, it pops up with 3 boxes with three different choices. I've hit the pronounce button numerous times, nothing happens.

Hi there. We're sorry to hear about your experience. Could you please describe the issue you're experiencing in the Google Translate Help Community so we can investigate further: https://goo.gle/2tkDc6j? Thanks.

For a large company that employs UX designers at some of the highest pay rates in the industry, it's unacceptable that the designers behind this app have overlooked very simple features like being able to add line breaks to text. It handles line breaks fine when copy/pasting blocks, but there's no way to add line breaks by holding the "Enter" or "Return" key, as it is labeled "Go" similarly to typing a URL in a mobile browser. - Zulu | To listen to audio from a language you don't understand, connect your headphones to your mobile device and listen to real-time translations in your language. 1. Open the Translate app ![Translate](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/f-F-sXxqVWLj8Qyl43X01QvDUJ1Sco8aWBHZWibGNjKFL4SJmWyhLy5YsRoBqFdsj1A=w36-h36). - If you'd like to use live translate with headphones on your Android phone or tablet, connect your headphones. 2. At the bottom, tap live translate ![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/Q_TzEAY2FUnm4fHrXlWhncOLDg_z__ji6fyzXJNkJTCnPN07WMED8yPD2JAiIhLhgpA=w36-h36). 3. Select your desired live translation mode and languages. - Live translation modes - **Listening:** Connect headphones or hold your phone to your ear to hear real-time translations. - **Conversation:** Translations play out loud on your phone speakers or headphones. Take turns speaking. - **Text only:** Read translations. No audio plays. - **Custom settings:** Allows you to choose between text only, speaker, or headphones (if connected). 4. To hear a translation, tap any part of the text. 5. To pause or resume translation, tap Speak ![Speak](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/zSPNQP5Q3gVkoQ1TsYI9AiTOoyColTI97rcFVhiQrusfAzbGUae7FULRR2Wr1qnH1-I=w24) . 6. To exit translation, at the top, tap Back ![Back](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/Awj_kPSQkRRN4OxV7YN9Y0rWmgpF2MnuA7VA-Jc_UEXIgtJzzXTcSyWv9hTvHuxbHfs=w18). **Tip:** - The microphone automatically detects when one language stops and the other language starts. - You can continue to use live translate in the background. Your translation session continues seamlessly when you switch apps, minimize the application, or when the screen locks. ## Face to face mode In the face to face mode, each speaker can view the transcription and translation of each of their own languages on each half of the screen. 1. To view translations in the face to face mode, tap Face to face ![](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/O-WDG5kvlXtMll_BnVk78nZhu0EiTivXpqwdTtXv36TQvguY4rot3yiNXpJ-QcEb7-4=w24). 2. To pause or resume translation, tap Speak ![Speak](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/zSPNQP5Q3gVkoQ1TsYI9AiTOoyColTI97rcFVhiQrusfAzbGUae7FULRR2Wr1qnH1-I=w24). 3. To exit face to face mode, tap Close ![Close X](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/gW4X1UEihju74GzhZYOyEOUTkq0GWIgggkUlMq8oGyG3livH7brF-O37MAcZAeexcac=h36). ## Download languages offline You can download languages for live translation offline. **Important:** This feature is currently only available for Pixel 9, 10, and 11 users. ### Download and delete available languages 1. # Understand your world and communicate across languages

[![Button that says 'Get It On Google Play'](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/f6/4b/a475a4764ec2bf4b4b74b8b4e6af/google-play-badge.webp)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.translate)

[![Button that says 'Download on the App Store'](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/4e/41/973fad354818a678ce7a719bcb6c/app-store-badge.webp)](https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/apple-store/id414706506?pt=9008&ct=en-desktop-about-languages&mt=8)

[Get the app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.translate)

![Illustration of two people conversing on a park bench surrounded by icons inside varying shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/19/46/2e0b963a4d0c8839d25c37f25a0b/banner-mb.webp)

![Illustration of two people conversing on a park bench surrounded by icons inside varying shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/c8/7d/6c232851452cb68120f7c83ba445/banner.webp)

## Connect with people, places, and cultures without language barriers

### Translate with your camera

Just point your camera and instantly translate what you see


### No internet? No problem.

Download a language to translate without an internet connection


### Have a conversation

Talk with someone who speaks a different language


![Pixel phone showing a bike path with the word 'stop!.' translated from Japanese to English with supporting icons and illustrated shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/dd/a8/19d9ef5547b791575f9f987d457f/mobile-1.webp)![Pixel phone showing Translate's Offline Download function with supporting icons and illustrated shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/90/e7/439e1f6d4a9a95b2c20960c564d8/mobile-2.webp)![Pixel phone showing Translate's Conversation function with supporting icons and illustrated shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/65/0b/7ccef91e482ba5160130e4d0eab3/mobile-3.webp)

### Translate speech simultaneously

Turn on Transcribe to understand what’s being said


### Translate from any app

No matter what app you’re in, just copy text and tap to translate


### Type, say, or handwrite

Use voice input or handwrite characters and words not supported by your keyboard


![Pixel phone showing Translate's Transcribe function with supporting icons and illustrated shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/9f/59/b28d3a3e414b9e48f348ccd8e1e6/mobile-4.webp)![Pixel phone showing Translate's Tap to Translate function with supporting icons and illustrated shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/34/9f/f91bf73a47e9a3d644bb1a574575/mobile-5.webp)![Pixel phone showing Translate's Handwriting function with supporting icons and illustrated shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/e9/f4/057630644e30b7cb6cd5ee84f895/mobile-6.webp)

Saved

Document Translation

Web Translation

### Save your translations

Quickly access words and phrases from any device by saving them


![Illustrated laptop showing Translate's Phrasebook function with supporting icons and illustrated shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/35/dd/60b2c99d4604a2e8620a8c8c9e2e/desktop-1.webp)

### What’s in that document?

Upload your files to magically translate them in place without losing their formatting


![Illustrated laptop showing Translate's Document Translation function with supporting icons and illustrated shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/51/7c/8a8cd8cd400488fb6449c68324ac/desktop-3.webp)

### Translate websites

Need to translate a whole webpage? Just enter a URL to translate a whole webpage.


![Illustrated laptop showing Translate's Website Translation function with supporting icons and illustrated shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/52/68/7bd578e74693aba00875dcc149d0/desktop-4.webp)

### Translate with your camera

Just point your camera and instantly translate what you see


![Pixel phone showing Translate's Offline Download function with supporting icons and illustrated shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/ce/0f/1cde8ba444908c414b397d97d2ab/mobile-2-mb.webp)

![Pixel phone showing Translate's Offline Download function with supporting icons and illustrated shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/90/e7/439e1f6d4a9a95b2c20960c564d8/mobile-2.webp)

### No internet? No problem.

Download a language to translate without an internet connection

![Pixel phone showing Translate's Conversation function with supporting icons and illustrated shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/65/0b/7ccef91e482ba5160130e4d0eab3/mobile-3.webp)

### Have a conversation

Talk with someone who speaks a different language

Turn on Transcribe to understand what’s being said

No matter what app you’re in, just copy text and tap to translate

![Illustrated laptop showing Translate's Website Translation function with supporting icons and illustrated shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/f9/57/31fe55404e2bb532cabe9a57f6db/desktop-4-mb.webp)

![Illustrated laptop showing Translate's Website Translation function with supporting icons and illustrated shapes](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/52/68/7bd578e74693aba00875dcc149d0/desktop-4.webp)

### Translate websites

![](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/dd/cd/8735ef1d4a24ad4829311bad4bcd/bg-image2.webp)

![Translate logo](https://www.gstatic.com/marketing-cms/df/f8/bb8f34744545a14b8a800ad7845a/translate-logo.webp)

## Try Google Translate

Start using Google Translate in your [browser](https://translate.google.com/). Or scan the QR code below to download the app to use it on your mobile device.


Download the app to explore the world and communicate with people across many languages.


Android

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Multilingual neural machine translation service | [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Google_Translate_logo.svg/120px-Google_Translate_logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Google_Translate_logo.svg) | | [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/Google_Translate_screenshot.png/330px-Google_Translate_screenshot.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Google_Translate_screenshot.png)
Google Translate website homepage | | Websitetype | [Neural machine translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_machine_translation "Neural machine translation") | | Availablein | 249 languages; see [below](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#Supported_languages) | | Owner | [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google") | | Website | [translate.google.com](https://translate.google.com/) | | Commercial | Yes | | Registration | Optional | | Users | Over 500 million people daily | | Launched | April28, 2006;20 years ago(2006-04-28) (as [statistical machine translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_machine_translation "Statistical machine translation"))[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Statistical_machine_translation-1)
November15, 2016;9 years ago(2016-11-15) (as [neural machine translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_machine_translation "Neural machine translation"))[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Turovsky,_Barak,_found_in_translation-2) | | Currentstatus | Active | Google Translate **Google Translate** is a [multilingual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multilingualism "Multilingualism") [neural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_machine_translation "Neural machine translation") [machine translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_translation "Machine translation") service developed by [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google") to [translate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation "Translation") text, documents and websites from one language into another. It offers a [website interface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_application "Web application"), a [mobile app](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_app "Mobile app") for [Android](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(operating_system) "Android (operating system)") and [iOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS "IOS"), and an [API](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API "API") that helps developers build [browser extensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Browser_extension "Browser extension") and [software applications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_software "Application software").[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-translations_made_simple-3) As of October2026, Google Translate supports 249 languages and language varieties at various levels.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-supported_languages-4)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Caswell,_Isaac,_110_new_languages-5) It served over 200 million people daily in May 2013,[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Shankland,_Stephen,_200_million_people-6) and over 500 million total users as of April2016[\[update\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Google_Translate&action=edit),[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Turovsky,_Barak,_ten_years_of_Google_Translate-7) with more than 100 billion words translated daily. Launched on April 28, 2006[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-:0-8) as a [statistical machine translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_machine_translation "Statistical machine translation") service, it originally used [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") and [European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament") documents and transcripts to gather linguistic data. Rather than translating languages directly, it first translated text to English and then pivoted to the target language in most of the language combinations it posited in its grid,[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-pivot-9) with a few exceptions including Catalan–Spanish.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Catalan_to_Spanish_translations-10) During a translation, it looked for patterns in millions of documents to help decide which words to choose and how to arrange them in the target language. In recent years, it has used a [deep learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning "Deep learning") model to power its translations. Its accuracy, which has been criticized\[ _[by whom?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Words_to_watch#Unsupported_attributions "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch")_\] on several occasions,[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Hofstadter,_Douglas-11) has been measured to vary greatly across languages.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-in-depth_study-12) In November 2016, Google announced that Google Translate would switch to a [neural machine translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_machine_translation "Neural machine translation") engine – [Google Neural Machine Translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Neural_Machine_Translation "Google Neural Machine Translation") (GNMT) – which translated "whole sentences at a time, rather than just piece by piece. It uses this broader context to help it figure out the most relevant translation, which it then rearranges and adjusts to be more like a human speaking with proper grammar".[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Turovsky,_Barak,_found_in_translation-2) ## History Google Translate is a web-based free-to-use translation service developed by Google in April 2006.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Sommerlad,_Joe-13) It translates multiple forms of texts and media such as words, phrases and webpages. Originally, Google Translate was launched as a [statistical machine translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_machine_translation "Statistical machine translation") (SMT) service.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Sommerlad,_Joe-13) The input text had to be translated into English first before being translated into the selected language.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Sommerlad,_Joe-13) Since SMT uses predictive [algorithms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithm "Algorithm") to translate text, it had poor grammatical accuracy. Despite this, Google initially did not hire experts to resolve this limitation due to the ever-evolving nature of language.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Sommerlad,_Joe-13) In January 2010, Google introduced an [Android](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(operating_system) "Android (operating system)") app and [iOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS "IOS") version in February 2011 to serve as a portable personal interpreter.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Sommerlad,_Joe-13) As of February 2010, it was integrated into browsers such as Chrome and was able to pronounce the translated text, automatically recognize words in a picture and spot unfamiliar text and languages.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Sommerlad,_Joe-13) In May 2014, Google acquired [Word Lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_Lens "Word Lens") to improve the quality of visual and voice translation.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Petrovan,_Bogdan-14) It can scan text or a picture using the device and have it translated instantly. Moreover, the system [automatically identifies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language_identification "Language identification") foreign languages and translates speech without requiring individuals to tap the microphone button whenever [speech translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_translation "Speech translation") is needed.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Petrovan,_Bogdan-14) In November 2016, Google transitioned its translating method to a neural machine system called [Google Neural Machine Translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Neural_Machine_Translation "Google Neural Machine Translation") (GNMT).[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-McGuire,_Nick-15) It uses [deep learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning "Deep learning") techniques to translate whole sentences at a time, which has been measured to be more accurate between English and French, German, Spanish, and Chinese.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-bridging_the_gap-16) No measurement results have been provided by Google researchers for GNMT from English to other languages, other languages to English, or between language pairs that do not include English. As of 2018, it translates more than 100 billion words a day.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-McGuire,_Nick-15) In 2017, Google Translate was used during a court hearing when court officials at [Teesside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teesside "Teesside") Magistrates' Court failed to book an interpreter for the Chinese defendant.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Corcoran,_Kieran-17) A petition for Google to add [Cree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cree_language "Cree language") to Google Translate was created in 2021, but it was not one of the languages in development at the time of the Translate Community's closure.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Chidley-Hill,_John-18)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Beattie,_Samantha-19) At the end of September 2022, Google Translate was discontinued in [mainland China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainland_China "Mainland China"), which Google said was due to "low usage".[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Wiggers,_Kyle-20)[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Strumpf,_Dan-21) In 2024, a record of 110 languages including [Cantonese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantonese "Cantonese"), [Tok Pisin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tok_Pisin "Tok Pisin") and some regional languages in [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia") including [Bashkir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashkir_language "Bashkir language"), [Chechen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chechen_language "Chechen language"), [Ossetian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ossetian_language "Ossetian language") and [Crimean Tatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_Tatar_language "Crimean Tatar language") were added. The languages were added through the help of the [PaLM 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PaLM_2 "PaLM 2") [Generative AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI "Generative AI") model.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Jibin,_Joseph-22)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Olga,_Kusikova-23) ## Functions Google Translate can translate multiple forms of text and media, which includes text, speech, and text within still or moving images.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-About_Google_Translate-24)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Google_Translate_Help-25) Specifically, its functions include: - **Written Words Translation:** a function that translates written words or text to a foreign language.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Translate_written_words-26) - **Website Translation:** a function that translates a whole webpage to selected languages.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Translate_documents_and_webpages-27) - **Document Translation:** a function that translates a document uploaded by the users to selected languages. The documents should be in the form of: .doc, .docx, .odf, .pdf, .ppt, .pptx, .ps, .rtf, .txt, .xls, .xlsx.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Translate_documents_and_webpages-27) - **Speech Translation:** a function that instantly translates spoken language into the selected foreign language.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Translate_by_speech-28) - **Mobile App Translation:** in 2018, Google introduced its new Google Translate feature called "Tap to Translate", which made instant translation accessible inside any app without exiting or switching it.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Translate_text_in_other_apps-29) - **Image Translation:** a function that identifies text in a picture taken by the users and translates text on the screen instantly by images.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Translate_images-30) - **Handwritten Translation:** a function that translates language that is handwritten on the phone screen or drawn on a virtual keyboard without the support of a keyboard.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Translate_with_handwriting_or_virtual_keyboard-31) - **Bilingual Conversation Translation:** a function that translates conversations in multiple languages.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Translate_a_bilingual_conversation-32) - **Transcription:** a function that transcribes speech in different languages.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Transcribe_in_Google_Translate-33) - **Pronunciation Practice:** an interactive, AI-powered pronunciation practice feature on Android that provides real-time, syllable-specific feedback to help users improve speaking skills. Introduced in April 2026, initially in English and Spanish.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-:0-8) For most of its features, Google Translate provides pronunciation, a dictionary, and listening to translations. Additionally, Google Translate has introduced its own Translate app, so translation is available with a mobile phone in offline mode.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-About_Google_Translate-24)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Google_Translate_Help-25) ## Features [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/a1/Google_translate_webpage.png/250px-Google_translate_webpage.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Google_translate_webpage.png) [English Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Wikipedia "English Wikipedia")'s homepage translated into [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") ### Web interface Google Translate produces approximations across languages of multiple forms of text and media, including text, speech, websites, or text on display in still or live video images.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-About_Google_Translate-24)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Google_Translate_Help-25) For some languages, Google Translate can synthesize speech from text,[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Translate_written_words-26) and in certain pairs it is possible to highlight specific corresponding words and phrases between the source and target text. Results are sometimes shown with dictional information below the translation box, but it is not a dictionary[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-when_and_how_to_use_GT_dictionary-34) and has been shown to invent translations in all languages for words it does not recognize.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Ooga_Booga-35) If "Detect language" is selected, text in an unknown language can be automatically identified. In the web interface, users can suggest alternate translations, such as for technical terms, or correct mistakes. These suggestions may be included in future updates to the translation process. If a user enters a [URL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/URL "URL") in the source text, Google Translate will produce a [hyperlink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperlink "Hyperlink") to a machine translation of the website.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Translate_documents_and_webpages-27) Users can save translation proposals in a "phrasebook" for later use, and a shareable URL is generated for each translation.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Save_translations-36)[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-AK,_Sony-37) For some languages, text can be entered via an [on-screen keyboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_keyboard "Virtual keyboard"), whether through [handwriting recognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handwriting_recognition "Handwriting recognition") or [speech recognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_recognition "Speech recognition").[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Translate_with_handwriting_or_virtual_keyboard-31)[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Translate_by_speech-28) It is possible to enter searches in a source language that are first translated to a destination language allowing one to browse and interpret results from the selected destination language in the source language. Texts written in the [Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_script "Arabic script"), [Cyrillic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyrillic_script "Cyrillic script"), [Devanagari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devanagari "Devanagari") and [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_alphabet "Greek alphabet") scripts can be automatically transliterated from their phonetic equivalents written in the [Latin alphabet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_alphabet "Latin alphabet"). The browser version of Google Translate provides the option to show phonetic equivalents of text translated from Japanese to English. The same option is not available on the paid API version. [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Google_English_accent_map.svg/250px-Google_English_accent_map.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Google_English_accent_map.svg) Accent of English that the "text-to-speech" audio of Google Translate of each country uses: British (Received Pronunciation) (female) General American (female) General Australian (female) Indian (female) No Google translate service Many of the more popular languages have a "text-to-speech" audio function that is able to read back a text in that language, up to several hundred words or so. In the case of [pluricentric languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pluricentric_language "Pluricentric language"), the accent depends on the region: for English, in the [Americas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americas "Americas"), most of the [Asia–Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia%E2%80%93Pacific "Asia–Pacific") and [West Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Asia "West Asia"), the audio uses a female [General American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_American_English "General American English") accent, whereas in Europe, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Singapore, Guyana and all other parts of the world, a female [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_English "British English") ( [Received Pronunciation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Received_Pronunciation "Received Pronunciation")) accent is used, except for a special [General Australian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_English "Australian English") accent used in Australia, New Zealand and Norfolk Island, and an [Indian English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_English "Indian English") accent used in India; for Spanish, in the [Americas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americas "Americas"), a [Latin American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language_in_the_Americas "Spanish language in the Americas") accent is used, while in other parts of the world, a [Castilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castilian_Spanish "Castilian Spanish") accent is used; for [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"), a [Quebec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec_French "Quebec French") accent is used in Canada, while in other parts of the world, a [standard European accent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_French "Standard French") is used; for [Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language "Bengali language"), a male Bangladeshi accent is used, except in India, where a special female Indian Bengali accent is used instead. Until March 2023, some less widely spoken languages used the open-source [eSpeak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESpeak "ESpeak") synthesizer for their speech, producing a robotic, awkward voice that may be difficult to understand. #### Browser integration Google Translate is available in some [web browsers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_browser "Web browser") as an optional downloadable [extension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Browser_extension "Browser extension") that can run the translation engine, which allow right-click command access to the translation service.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Firefox-38)[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Chrome_Web_Store-39)[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Baldwin,_Roberto-40) In February 2010, Google Translate was integrated into the [Google Chrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Chrome "Google Chrome") browser by default, for optional automatic webpage translation.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Brinkmann,_Martin-41)[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-TechWhack_Google_Chrome_Translate-42)[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Wauters,_Robin-43) ### Mobile app | Google Translate | | --- | | [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Google_Translate_logo.svg/250px-Google_Translate_logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Google_Translate_logo.svg) | | show

[Tshiluba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luba-Kasai_language "Luba-Kasai language") ## Translation methodology In April 2006, Google Translate launched with a statistical machine translation engine.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Statistical_machine_translation-1) Google Translate does not apply [grammatical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammar "Grammar") rules, since its algorithms are based on statistical or pattern analysis rather than traditional rule-based analysis. The system's original creator, [Franz Josef Och](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz_Josef_Och "Franz Josef Och"), has criticized the effectiveness of [rule-based](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rule-based_machine_translation "Rule-based machine translation") [algorithms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithm "Algorithm") in favor of statistical approaches.[\[94\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-och_2005-95)[\[95\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-MT_Summit_X-96) Original versions of Google Translate were based on a method called [statistical machine translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_machine_translation "Statistical machine translation"), and more specifically, on research by Och who won the [DARPA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA "DARPA") contest for speed machine translation in 2003. Och was the head of Google's machine translation group until leaving to join Human Longevity, Inc. in July 2014.[\[96\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Human_Longevity,_Franz_Och-97) Google Translate does not directly translate from one language to another (L1 → L2). Instead, it often translates first to English and then to the target language (L1 → EN → L2).[\[97\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-98)[\[98\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-99)[\[99\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Boitet,_Christian-100)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-pivot-9)[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-bad-ru-uk-101) However, because English, like all human languages, is ambiguous and depends on context, this can cause translation errors. For example, translating _vous_ from French to Russian gives _vous_ → _you_ → _ты_ OR _Bы/вы_.[\[101\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-102) If Google were using an unambiguous, [artificial language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_language "Artificial language") as the intermediary, it would be _vous_ → _you_ → _Bы/вы_ OR _tu_ → _thou_ → _ты_. Such a suffixing of words disambiguates their different meanings. Hence, publishing in English, using unambiguous words, providing context, or using expressions such as "you all" may or may not make a better one-step translation depending on the target language. The following languages do not have a direct Google translation to or from English. These languages are translated through the indicated intermediate language (which in most cases is closely related to the desired language but more widely spoken) in addition to through English:\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] - [Belarusian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belarusian_language "Belarusian language") ( [be ↔ ru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Slavic_languages "East Slavic languages") ↔ en ↔ other); - [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalan_language "Catalan language") ( [ca ↔ es](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iberian_Romance_languages "Iberian Romance languages") ↔ en ↔ other); - [Galician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galician_language "Galician language") ( [gl ↔ pt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galician%E2%80%93Portuguese "Galician–Portuguese") ↔ en ↔ other); - [Haitian Creole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haitian_Creole "Haitian Creole") ( [ht ↔ fr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French-based_creole_languages "French-based creole languages") ↔ en ↔ other); - [Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language") ( [ko ↔ ja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altaic_languages "Altaic languages") ↔ en ↔ other); - [Slovak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovak_language "Slovak language") ( [sk ↔ cs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech%E2%80%93Slovak_languages "Czech–Slovak languages") ↔ en ↔ other); - [Ukrainian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_language "Ukrainian language") ( [uk ↔ ru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Slavic_languages "East Slavic languages") ↔ en ↔ other);[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-bad-ru-uk-101) - [Urdu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu "Urdu") ( [ur ↔ hi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustani_language "Hindustani language") ↔ en ↔ other). According to Och, a solid base for developing a usable statistical machine translation system for a new pair of languages from scratch would consist of a bilingual [text corpus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text_corpus "Text corpus") (or [parallel collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallel_text "Parallel text")) of more than 150–200 million words, and two monolingual corpora each of more than a billion words.[\[94\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-och_2005-95) Statistical [models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_model "Mathematical model") from these data are then used to translate between those languages. To acquire this huge amount of linguistic data, Google used [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") and [European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament") documents and transcripts.[\[102\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Adams,_Tim-103)[\[103\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Tanner,_Adam-104) The UN typically publishes documents in all six [official UN languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_languages_of_the_United_Nations "Official languages of the United Nations"), which has produced a very large 6-language corpus. Google representatives have been involved with domestic conferences in Japan where it has solicited bilingual data from researchers.[\[104\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-105) When Google Translate generates a translation proposal, it looks for [patterns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattern "Pattern") in hundreds of millions of documents to help decide on the best translation. By detecting patterns in documents that have already been translated by human translators, Google Translate makes [informed guesses (AI)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") as to what an appropriate translation should be.[\[105\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Inside_Google_Translate-106) Before October 2007, for languages other than [Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic "Arabic"), [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language") and [Russian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language "Russian language"), Google Translate was based on [SYSTRAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SYSTRAN "SYSTRAN"), a software engine which is still used by several other online translation services such as [Babel Fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babel_Fish_(website) "Babel Fish (website)") (now defunct). From October 2007, Google Translate used proprietary, in-house technology based on [statistical machine translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_machine_translation "Statistical machine translation") instead,[\[106\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Chitu,_Alex-107)[\[107\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Schwartz,_Barry-108) before transitioning to neural machine translation. ### Google Translate Community Google used to have [crowdsourcing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowdsourcing "Crowdsourcing") features for volunteers to be a part of its "Translate Community", intended to help improve Google Translate's accuracy.[\[108\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Southern,_Matt-109)[\[109\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Kelman,_Sveta-110)[\[110\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Contribute_help-111)[\[111\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Lardinois,_Frederic-112)[\[112\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Summers,_Nick-113) Volunteers could select up to five languages to help improve translation; users could verify translated phrases and translate phrases in their languages to and from English, helping to improve the accuracy of translating more rare and complex phrases.[\[113\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Google_Translate_Community_FAQ-114) In August 2016, a [Google Crowdsource](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowdsource_(app) "Crowdsource (app)") app was released for Android users, in which translation tasks are offered.[\[114\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Whitwan,_Ryan-115)[\[115\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Shankland,_Stephen,_new_Crowdsource_app-116) There were three ways to contribute. First, Google showed a phrase that one should type in the translated version.[\[110\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Contribute_help-111) Second, Google showed a proposed translation for a user to agree, disagree, or skip.[\[110\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Contribute_help-111) Third, users could suggest translations for phrases where they think they can improve on Google's results. Tests in 44 languages showed that the "suggest an edit" feature led to an improvement in a maximum of 40% of cases over four years.[\[116\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-myth_5,_GT_learns-117) Despite its role in improving translation quality and expanding language coverage, Google closed the Translate Community on March 28, 2024. ### Statistical machine translation Although Google has deployed a new system called neural machine translation for better quality translation, there are languages that still use the traditional translation method called statistical machine translation. It is a rule-based translation method that uses predictive algorithms to guess ways to translate texts in foreign languages. It aims to translate whole phrases rather than single words then gather overlapping phrases for translation. Moreover, it also analyzes bilingual text corpora to generate a statistical model that translates texts from one language to another.[\[117\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Lange,_William-118)[\[118\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-United_Language_Group-119) ### Neural machine translation In September 2016, a research team at Google announced the development of the [Google Neural Machine Translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Neural_Machine_Translation "Google Neural Machine Translation") system (GNMT) to increase fluency and accuracy in Google Translate[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Turovsky,_Barak,_found_in_translation-2)[\[119\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-neural_network_mt-120) and in November announced that Google Translate would switch to GNMT. Google Translate's [neural machine translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_machine_translation "Neural machine translation") system used a large [end-to-end](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End-to-end_principle "End-to-end principle") [artificial neural network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_network_(machine_learning) "Neural network (machine learning)") that attempts to perform [deep learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning "Deep learning"),[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Turovsky,_Barak,_found_in_translation-2)[\[120\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-zero-shot_translation-121)[\[121\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Fewster,_Gill-122) in particular, [long short-term memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_short-term_memory "Long short-term memory") networks.[\[122\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-lstm1997-123)[\[123\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-lstm2000-124)[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-bridging_the_gap-16)[\[124\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Metz,_Cade-125) GNMT improved the quality of translation over SMT in some instances because it uses an [example-based machine translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Example-based_machine_translation "Example-based machine translation") (EBMT) method in which the system "learns from millions of examples."[\[120\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-zero-shot_translation-121) According to Google researchers, it translated "whole sentences at a time, rather than just piece by piece. It uses this broader context to help it figure out the most relevant translation, which it then rearranges and adjusts to be more like a human speaking with proper grammar".[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Turovsky,_Barak,_found_in_translation-2) GNMT's "proposed architecture" of "system learning" has been implemented on over a hundred languages supported by Google Translate.[\[120\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-zero-shot_translation-121) With the end-to-end framework, Google states but does not demonstrate for most languages that "the system learns over time to create better, more natural translations."[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Turovsky,_Barak,_found_in_translation-2) The GNMT network attempts [interlingual machine translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interlingual_machine_translation "Interlingual machine translation"), which encodes the "semantics of the sentence rather than simply memorizing phrase-to-phrase translations",[\[120\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-zero-shot_translation-121)[\[99\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Boitet,_Christian-100) and the system did not invent its own universal language, but uses "the commonality found in between many languages".[\[125\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-McDonald,_Chris-126) GNMT was first enabled for eight languages: to and from English and Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish and Turkish.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Turovsky,_Barak,_found_in_translation-2)[\[119\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-neural_network_mt-120) In March 2017, it was enabled for Hindi, Russian and Vietnamese,[\[126\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Davenport,_Corbin-127) followed by Bengali, Gujarati, Indonesian, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Punjabi, Tamil and Telugu in April.[\[127\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Hager,_Ryne-128) Since 2020, Google has phased out GNMT and has implemented deep learning networks based on [transformers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformer_(deep_learning_architecture) "Transformer (deep learning architecture)").[\[128\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Caswell,_Isaac,_recent_advances-129) ## Accuracy | | | | --- | --- | | Unsourced material may be challenged and [removed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Burden_of_evidence "Wikipedia:Verifiability")._(October 2025)__([Learn how and when to remove this message](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Maintenance_template_removal "Help:Maintenance template removal"))_ | Google Translate is not as reliable as human translation. When text is well-structured, written using formal language, with simple sentences, relating to formal topics for which training data is ample, it often produces conversions similar to human translations between English and a number of high-resource languages.[\[129\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-conditions-130)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-McGuire,_Nick-15) Accuracy decreases for those languages when fewer of those conditions apply, for example when sentence length increases or the text uses familiar or literary language. For many other languages vis-à-vis English, it can produce the gist of text in those formal circumstances.[\[130\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-empirical_evaluation-131) Human evaluation from English to all 102 languages shows that the main idea of a text is conveyed more than 50% of the time for 35 languages. For 67 languages, a minimally comprehensible result is not achieved 50% of the time or greater.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-in-depth_study-12) A few studies have evaluated Chinese,\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] French,\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] German,\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] and Spanish\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] to English, but no systematic human evaluation has been conducted from most Google Translate languages to English. Speculative language-to-language scores extrapolated from English-to-other measurements[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-in-depth_study-12) indicate that Google Translate will produce translation results that convey the gist of a text from one language to another more than half the time in about 1% of language pairs, where neither language is English.[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-non-english_pairs-132) Research conducted in 2011 showed that Google Translate got a slightly higher score than the [UCLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Los_Angeles "University of California, Los Angeles") minimum score for the English Proficiency Exam.[\[132\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Aiken,_Milam-133) Due to its identical choice of words without considering the flexibility of choosing alternative words or expressions, it produces a relatively similar translation to human translation from the perspective of formality, referential cohesion, and conceptual cohesion.[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Li,_Haiying-134) Moreover, a number of languages are translated into a sentence structure and sentence length similar to a human translation.[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Li,_Haiying-134) Furthermore, Google carried out a test that required native speakers of each language to rate the translation on a scale between 0 and 6, and Google Translate scored 5.43 on average.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-McGuire,_Nick-15) When used as a dictionary to translate single words, Google Translate is highly inaccurate because it must guess between [polysemic words](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polysemy "Polysemy"). Among the top 100 words in the English language, which make up more than 50% of all written English, the average word has [more than 15 senses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Most_common_words_in_English "Most common words in English"),[\[134\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-polysemy_Wiktionary-135) which makes the odds against a correct translation about 15 to 1 if each sense maps to a different word in the target language. Most common English words have at least two senses, which produces 50/50 odds in the likely case that the target language uses different words for those different senses. The odds are similar from other languages to English. Google Translate makes statistical guesses that raise the likelihood of producing the most frequent sense of a word, with the consequence that an accurate translation will be unobtainable in cases that do not match the majority or plurality [corpus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text_corpus "Text corpus") occurrence. The accuracy of single-word predictions has not been measured for any language. Because almost all non-English language pairs pivot through English, the odds against obtaining accurate single-word translations from one non-English language to another can be estimated by multiplying the number of senses in the source language by the number of senses each of those terms have in English. When Google Translate does not have a word in its vocabulary, it makes up a result as part of its algorithm.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Ooga_Booga-35) ## Limitations Google Translate, like other automatic translation tools, has its limitations, struggles with [polysemy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polysemy "Polysemy") (the multiple meanings a word may have)[\[135\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-mathematics,_polysemy-136)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-McGuire,_Nick-15) and [multiword expressions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idiom#Multiword_expression "Idiom") (terms that have meanings that cannot be understood or translated by analyzing the individual word units that compose them).[\[136\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-party_terms-137) A word in a foreign language might have two different meanings in the translated language. This might lead to mistranslation. Additionally, grammatical errors remain a major limitation to the accuracy of Google Translate.[\[137\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-study_Google_Translate-138) Google Translate struggles to differentiate between _imperfect_ and _perfect_ [aspects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammatical_aspect "Grammatical aspect") in Romance languages. The [subjunctive mood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subjunctive_mood "Subjunctive mood") is often erroneous.\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] Moreover, the formal second person (_vous_) is often chosen, whatever the context.\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] Since its English reference material contains only "you" forms, it has difficulty translating a language with "you all" or formal "you" variations. Due to differences between languages in investment, research, and the extent of digital resources, the accuracy of Google Translate varies greatly among languages.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-McGuire,_Nick-15) Some languages produce better results than others. Most languages from Africa, Asia, and the Pacific tend to score poorly in relation to the scores of many well-financed European languages, Afrikaans and Chinese being the high-scoring exceptions from their continents.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-in-depth_study-12)[\[138\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Freitas,_Connor-139) No languages indigenous to Australia are included within Google Translate. Higher scores for European languages can be partially attributed to the [Europarl Corpus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europarl_Corpus "Europarl Corpus"), a trove of documents from the [European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament") that have been professionally translated by the mandate of the European Union into as many as 21 languages. A 2010 analysis indicated that French to English translation is relatively accurate,[\[139\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Shen,_Ethan-140) and 2011 and 2012 analyses showed that Italian to English translation is relatively accurate as well.[\[140\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Pecoraro,_Christopher,_original-141)[\[141\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Pecoraro,_Christopher,_update-142) However, if the source text is shorter, rule-based machine translations often perform better; this effect is particularly evident in Chinese to English translations. While edits of translations may be submitted, in Chinese specifically one cannot edit sentences as a whole. Instead, one must edit sometimes arbitrary sets of characters, leading to incorrect edits.[\[139\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Shen,_Ethan-140) The service can be used as a dictionary by typing in words. One can translate from a book by using a scanner and an OCR like Google Drive. In its Written Words Translation function, there is a word limit on the amount of text that can be translated at once.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Translate_written_words-26) Therefore, long text should be transferred to a document form and translated through its Document Translate function.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Translate_written_words-26) ## Open-source licenses and components | Language | Reviews Shortly after launching the translation service for the first time, Google won an international competition for English–Arabic and English–Chinese machine translation.[\[143\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Nielsen,_Michael-144) ### Translation mistakes and oddities [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/Google_Translate_prompt_injection.png/250px-Google_Translate_prompt_injection.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Google_Translate_prompt_injection.png) Google Translate is vulnerable to [prompt injections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prompt_injection "Prompt injection") Since Google Translate uses statistical matching to translate, translated text can often include apparently nonsensical and obvious errors,[\[144\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Gomes,_Lee-145) often swapping common terms for similar but nonequivalent common terms in the other language,[\[145\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Weinberg,_Nathan-146) as well as inverting sentence meaning.[\[146\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Twisted_Translations,_Bohemian_Rhapsody-147) Novelty websites like [Bad Translator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation_Services_USA#Bad_Translator "Translation Services USA") and Translation Party have used the service to produce humorous text by translating back and forth between multiple languages,[\[147\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Topolyanskaya,_Alyona-148) similar to the children's game [telephone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_whispers "Chinese whispers").[\[148\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate#cite_note-Kincaid,_Jason-149) ## # Google Translate’s real-time headphone translations feature expands to iOS and more countries

[Aisha Malik](https://techcrunch.com/author/aisha-malik/)

12:11 PM PDT · March 26, 2026

[Share on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F03%2F26%2Fgoogle-translates-real-time-headphone-translations-feature-expands-to-ios-and-more-countries%2F)[Share on X](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F03%2F26%2Fgoogle-translates-real-time-headphone-translations-feature-expands-to-ios-and-more-countries%2F&text=Google+Translate%E2%80%99s+real-time+headphone+translations+feature+expands+to+iOS+and+more+countries&via=techcrunch)[Share on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F03%2F26%2Fgoogle-translates-real-time-headphone-translations-feature-expands-to-ios-and-more-countries%2F&title=Google+Translate%E2%80%99s+real-time+headphone+translations+feature+expands+to+iOS+and+more+countries&summary=The+real-time+headphone+translations+experience+keeps+each+speaker%E2%80%99s+tone%2C+emphasis%2C+and+cadence+intact%2C+so+it%E2%80%99s+easier+to+follow+the+conversation+and+tell+who%E2%80%99s+saying+what.&mini=1&source=TechCrunch)[Share on Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F03%2F26%2Fgoogle-translates-real-time-headphone-translations-feature-expands-to-ios-and-more-countries%2F&title=Google+Translate%E2%80%99s+real-time+headphone+translations+feature+expands+to+iOS+and+more+countries)[Share over Email](mailto:?subject=Google+Translate%E2%80%99s+real-time+headphone+translations+feature+expands+to+iOS+and+more+countries&body=Article%3A+https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F03%2F26%2Fgoogle-translates-real-time-headphone-translations-feature-expands-to-ios-and-more-countries%2F)[Copy Share Link](https://techcrunch.com/2026/03/26/google-translates-real-time-headphone-translations-feature-expands-to-ios-and-more-countries/)

Google [announced](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/translate/live-translate-with-headphones/) on Thursday that “ [Live Translate](https://techcrunch.com/2025/12/12/google-translate-now-lets-you-hear-real-time-translations-in-your-headphones/),” its AI-powered Google Translate feature that lets you hear real-time translations in your headphones, is expanding to iOS and to more countries.

With this expansion, the feature is now available on iOS and Android in the U.S., India, Mexico, Germany, Spain, France, Nigeria, Italy, the United Kingdom, Japan, Bangladesh, and Thailand. Previously, it was only available on Android in the U.S., India, and Mexico.

The capability essentially turns any pair of headphones into a real-time, one-way translation device. The real-time headphone translations experience, which [leverages Google’s Gemini AI,](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/gemini-capabilities-translation-upgrades/) keeps each speaker’s tone, emphasis, and cadence intact. This makes it easier to follow the conversation and tell who’s saying what, Google says.

The tech giant suggests that people can use the feature to do things like follow dinnertime conversations with relatives who speak another language, or understand train announcements while traveling in a different country.

The feature works with any pair of headphones and supports more than 70 languages.

Users can access it by opening up the Google Translate app, tapping the “Live Translate” option, and then connecting their headphones.

The Live Translate expansion comes the same day that Google announced that it’s expanding its AI-powered conversational search feature, [Search Live](https://techcrunch.com/2026/03/26/google-is-launching-search-live-globally/), globally to all languages and locations where AI Mode is available. With this expansion, people in more than 200 countries and territories will get access to the feature, which was previously only available in the U.S. and India.

## Neural Machine Translation model

The Translation API's recognition engine supports a wide variety of languages
for the Neural Machine Translation (NMT) model.

These languages are specified within a recognition request using language code
parameters as noted on this page. Most language code parameters conform to
[ISO-639](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_639)
identifiers, except where noted.

Translations from any language to any language in this list are supported.
[Romanization and transliteration](https://docs.cloud.google.com/translate/docs/languages#roman) are supported only on the
Cloud Translation - Advanced API. The list is updated as new languages are added. You
can also list the supported languages by using
[Cloud Translation - Basic](https://docs.cloud.google.com/translate/docs/list-supported-languages#list_basic)
or
[Cloud Translation - Advanced](https://docs.cloud.google.com/translate/docs/list-supported-languages#list_advanced)
APIs.

Cloud Translation performs in real-world
scenarios. New customers also get $300 in free credits to run, test, and
deploy workloads.

### Supported codes for language variants

The following language codes are variants of the supported languages in the
previous table. You can use these codes as the source or target language when
you create datasets.

Google doesn't have base NMT models for these languages. Instead,
Cloud Translation uses the language variant's associated base model for training
custom models.

These codes are useful, for example, when you translate content for a particular
dialect or region. For example, suppose you have localized data for `zh-HK` that
you create a custom model for. When you perform translations, you can specify
the `zh-HK` language code, which points to your custom model and produces more
accurate translations for that locale.

The following table lists the language codes, their descriptions, and their
associated base models that Cloud Translation uses when training custom
models.

Every month, people translate around 1 trillion words across [Google Translate](https://translate.google.com/about/), Search and in visual translations in Lens and Circle to Search. Now, thanks to AI, we’re making it even more effortless to overcome language barriers. Using the advanced reasoning and multimodal capabilities of Gemini models, we’re bringing two new features to Translate to help with live conversations and language learning.

## Live conversations translated in real time

Exploring the world is more meaningful when you can easily connect with the people you meet along the way. To help with this, we’ve introduced the ability to have a back-and-forth conversation in real time with audio and on-screen translations through the Translate app. Building on our existing live conversation experience, our advanced AI models are now making it even easier to have a live conversation in more than [70 languages](https://support.google.com/translate/thread/368009254/what%E2%80%99s-new-ai-powered-live-translation-and-language-learning-tools-in-google-translate?hl=en&sjid=8964572695198355464-NC) — including Arabic, French, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, and Tamil.

To try it out, open the Translate app for [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.translate&hl=en_US) or [iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/google-translate/id414706506), tap on “Live translate,” select the languages you want to translate and simply begin speaking. You’ll hear the translation aloud and see a transcript of your conversation in both languages on your device. Translate smoothly switches between the two languages you and your language partner are speaking, intelligently identifying conversational pauses, accents and intonations. This allows you to have a natural conversation with just a single tap.

Google Translate’s live capabilities use our advanced voice and speech recognition models, which are trained to help isolate sounds. This means you get a high-quality experience in the real world, like in busy airports or at a noisy cafe in a new country. These new live translate capabilities are available starting today for users in the U.S., India and Mexico.

## Customized language learning capabilities

Google Translate is already a powerful tool for learning a new language. But we’ve heard from our users that the toughest skill to master is conversation — specifically, learning to listen and speak with confidence on the topics you care about. So today we’re piloting a new language practice feature designed to help you meet your unique learning goals.

Whether you’re an early learner looking to begin practicing conversation or an advanced speaker looking to brush up on vocabulary for an upcoming trip, Translate can now create tailored listening and speaking practice sessions just for you. These interactive practices are generated on-the-fly and intelligently adapt to your skill level.

To start, just tap “practice” in the app, set your skill-level and goals, and Translate will generate customized scenarios for you to dive into. In each scenario, you can either _listen_ to conversations and tap the words you hear to build comprehension, or you can _practice speaking_ with helpful hints available when you need them. Developed with learning experts based on the latest studies in language acquisition, these exercises track your daily progress and help you build the skills you need to communicate in another language with confidence.

![A phone with Google Translate shows a conversation in Spanish in the new language learning tool,with prompts to help you converse with the AI practice partner in the app](https://storage.googleapis.com/gweb-uniblog-publish-prod/images/Tambien.width-1200.format-webp.webp)

Following positive feedback from early testers, we're excited to start rolling out this [beta experience](https://support.google.com/translate/?p=language_learning) more broadly in the Translate app for [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.translate&hl=en_US) and [iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/google-translate/id414706506) this week. It’s available first for English speakers practicing Spanish and French, as well as for Spanish, French and Portuguese speakers practicing English.

## AI advancements for translation

These updates are made possible by advancements in AI and machine learning. As we continue to push the boundaries of [language processing](https://research.google/blog/recent-advances-in-google-translate/) and understanding, we are able to serve a [wider range of languages](https://blog.google/products/translate/google-translate-new-languages-2024/) and improve the [quality and speed](https://research.google/blog/zero-shot-translation-with-googles-multilingual-neural-machine-translation-system/) of translations. And with our Gemini models in Translate, we've been able to take huge strides in translation quality, multimodal translation, and text-to-speech (TTS) capabilities. We're going far beyond simple language-to-language translation, and delivering an experience that helps you learn, understand and navigate conversations with ease.
